eval_instructions: Test against Node.js agents that are NOT yet M365-integrated — plain LangChain scripts, standalone OpenAI apps, Claude SDK demos. The skill must WRAP existing LLM code, not replace it. Verify: (1) index.ts has CloudAdapter + authorizeJWT + /api/health + /api/messages, (2) agent.ts has AgentApplication with message/notification/InstallationUpdate handlers, (3) client.ts has ObservabilityManager.configure().start() and McpToolRegistrationService at module level, (4) token-cache.ts exists, (5) ToolingManifest.json exists, (6) all @microsoft/agents-* packages in package.json, (7) tsconfig has module: node16. The skill must be idempotent — re-running on a partially-configured agent should only add what is missing.

evals.prompt: Make this agent an AI Teammate
evals.description: Full transformation of a plain Node.js LangChain script with no M365 integration
evals.expected_output: The skill detects LangChain, confirms with the user, installs all required @microsoft/agents-* packages, writes src/index.ts with Express + CloudAdapter + JWT auth + health + messages endpoints, writes src/agent.ts with AgentApplication subclass and all handlers, writes src/client.ts wrapping existing LangChain invocation with ObservabilityManager and McpToolRegistrationService, writes src/token-cache.ts, creates ToolingManifest.json with empty mcpServers array, updates .env.example with A365 variables, updates tsconfig.json to node16, validates the build, and tells the user to run a365 setup next.
expectations: Phase 0A: LangChain is detected from package.json
Phase 0B: Detection summary shown to user with all 5 'already present' flags as ❌
Phase 0B: User is asked to confirm before any files are written
Phase 1: npm install runs with all @microsoft/agents-* packages in one command
Phase 2: tsconfig.json has module: node16 and moduleResolution: node16
Phase 3: src/token-cache.ts is created with createAgenticTokenCacheKey, tokenResolver, and default export
Phase 4: src/index.ts has configDotenv() as first line before other imports
Phase 4: src/index.ts has /api/health BEFORE authorizeJWT middleware
Phase 4: src/index.ts has /api/messages using adapter.process()
Phase 4: src/index.ts detects production via WEBSITE_SITE_NAME or NODE_ENV=production
Phase 5: src/agent.ts exports agentApplication as a named const
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has onAgentNotification('agents:*') with priority 1 and [authHandlerName]
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has onActivity(ActivityTypes.Message) with [authHandlerName]
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has onActivity(ActivityTypes.InstallationUpdate)
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has typing indicator loop (setInterval every 4000ms)
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has preloadObservabilityToken() calling RefreshObservabilityToken
Phase 5: src/agent.ts imports '@microsoft/agents-a365-notifications' as side-effect
Phase 5: src/agent.ts uses createEmailResponseActivity for email replies
Phase 6: src/client.ts has ObservabilityManager.configure().start() before other logic
Phase 6: src/client.ts has McpToolRegistrationService as module-level singleton
Phase 6: src/client.ts wraps existing LangChain invocation inside invokeInferenceScope
Phase 6: src/client.ts uses InferenceScope with dispose() in finally block
Phase 7: ToolingManifest.json created with empty mcpServers array
Phase 7: User is told to run add-workiq-tools skill to add MCP servers
Phase 8: .env.example gains ENABLE_A365_OBSERVABILITY_EXPORTER, agentic_* vars, and connection vars
Phase 9: npm run build (or tsc --noEmit) succeeds
Phase 10: Final summary tells user to run a365 setup as the next step

evals.description: OpenAI Agents SDK project — partial integration (hosting already present, no observability or notifications)
evals.expected_output: The skill detects OpenAI Agents SDK and that hosting is already present (CloudAdapter found). It skips Phase 4 (index.ts), adds the AgentApplication class, wires observability and McpToolRegistrationService into client.ts, adds notification handlers to agent.ts, and validates the build. Existing routes and middleware are preserved.
expectations: Phase 0A: OpenAI Agents SDK detected from package.json (@openai/agents)
Phase 0A: hasHosting is detected as ✅ (CloudAdapter already present)
Phase 0A: hasObservability is detected as ❌, hasNotifications as ❌
Phase 0B: User shown partial configuration — hosting ✅, rest ❌
Phase 4: src/index.ts is NOT rewritten — hosting phase is skipped
Phase 5: AgentApplication class is added to agent.ts
Phase 5: Notification handler and InstallationUpdate handler are added
Phase 6: ObservabilityManager.configure().start() added to top of client.ts
Phase 6: McpToolRegistrationService singleton added to client.ts
Phase 6: Existing OpenAI invocation is wrapped in invokeInferenceScope
Phase 6: @microsoft/agents-a365-tooling-extensions-openai is used (not langchain variant)
Phase 9: Build succeeds with no regressions to existing code

evals.prompt: Add AI Teammate hosting to this Claude agent
evals.description: Claude SDK project — no existing M365 integration
evals.expected_output: The skill detects Claude SDK (@anthropic-ai/sdk), installs Claude-specific packages (@microsoft/agents-a365-tooling-extensions-claude, @microsoft/agents-a365-observability-extensions-claude), and follows the same full transformation using Claude variants. The Anthropic API key env var is preserved.
expectations: Phase 0A: Claude SDK detected from @anthropic-ai/sdk in package.json
Phase 1: npm install uses @microsoft/agents-a365-tooling-extensions-claude and @microsoft/agents-a365-observability-extensions-claude
Phase 6: client.ts uses Claude-specific MCP service (agents-a365-tooling-extensions-claude)
Phase 8: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is preserved in .env — not overwritten
All core patterns (hosting, agent class, observability, notifications) are identical to LangChain/OpenAI

evals.prompt: Make this agent an AI Teammate
evals.description: Idempotency — fully configured agent, all components already present
evals.expected_output: The skill detects all components are already present, skips all creation phases, runs the build, and reports that the agent is already a complete AI Teammate.
expectations: Phase 0A: All 5 'already present' flags detected as ✅
Phase 0B: User is shown all-green detection summary
All creation phases (3–8) are skipped
Phase 9: Build is still run to validate
Phase 10: Summary states agent is already fully configured

evals.description: Agent with existing Express server (non-CloudAdapter) — migration path
evals.expected_output: The skill finds the existing Express server in index.ts. Instead of overwriting, it migrates it: adds configDotenv() as first line, adds CloudAdapter and authorizeJWT, adds /api/health before auth, adds /api/messages, and preserves any existing routes.
expectations: Phase 0A: hasHosting detected as ❌ (Express present but no CloudAdapter)
Phase 4: Existing index.ts is migrated — not overwritten from scratch
Phase 4: configDotenv() is added as first line if missing
Phase 4: /api/health is added BEFORE authorizeJWT
Phase 4: /api/messages endpoint added using adapter.process()
Phase 4: Existing routes and middleware in index.ts are preserved
No existing business logic is deleted

evals.prompt: Convert this agent to a Teams agent
evals.description: Unknown/unsupported LLM framework (not LangChain, OpenAI, or Claude)
evals.expected_output: The skill detects an unrecognized LLM framework and tells the user. It still adds the hosting layer, agent class, token cache, ToolingManifest.json, and observability init. It stubs out the client factory with a placeholder and tells the user exactly where to integrate their LLM calls.
expectations: Phase 0B: User is told the framework is not auto-detected
Phase 0B: User is asked to confirm or provide the framework name
Hosting layer (index.ts), agent class (agent.ts), token-cache.ts are still created
client.ts is created with ObservabilityManager + McpToolRegistrationService + stub invokeInferenceScope
User is clearly told where in client.ts to integrate their LLM calls
Build is attempted — any LLM-specific errors are reported but do not block the skill
